new_statements.rule_in_words: Barzani, like all NENA dialects outside the Trans-Zab Jewish group, has word stress generally on the penultimate syllable (stated for nominal forms); the fieldworker who described Barzani transcribes his Barzani/Sandu data with penultimate stress as the unmarked default, marking only deviations.
new_statements.exceptions: The 2008 statement is scoped to 'nominal forms' ('generally penultimate'); deviations from penultimate stress are marked ad hoc in transcription ('unless otherwise indicated'); no Barzani-specific exceptions are discussed in either open source.
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical stress; the explicit typological statement concerns the nominal system. Both statements are by Hezy Mutzafi, the only fieldworker to have described Barzani (1996-2000 fieldwork), but neither is a Barzani-specific phonology section: the 2008 sentence is a group-level claim over 'all other known NENA dialects' (Barzani explicitly among them in the same article), and the 2025 sentence is a transcription convention for his Sandu and Barzani data. The dedicated sketch (Mutzafi 2002, MLR 14) could refine this (e.g. verbal forms, enclitics, loanwords) and was not accessible.
new_statements.identity_note: Barzani Jewish Neo-Aramaic = the 'Barzani cluster' of three village dialects, Barzan, Shahe and Bijil (Bejil), near Aqra, NW Iraq (Glottolog barz1241, ISO bjf); Mutzafi 2025 groups it with Sandu as the 'Barzani-Sandu / Central Jewish NA' subgroup of NENA, between Lishana Deni (lish1247) and Trans-Zab. The quoted 2008 statement is a NENA-wide claim (all non-Trans-Zab dialects) in which Barzani is explicitly enumerated; the 2025 transcription note covers the author's Sandu and Barzani fieldwork data. Only the Barzan village dialect survived to 2024 (four passive speakers); Bijil extinct 1998.
